articleTitle: Skin Cancer Diagnosis and Detection Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: If early diagnosis and early detection of skin cancer is achieved, many patients can survive. The traditional method for the public has always suffered from problems such as imprecision and biased results. This study therefore presents a method that can be introduced in a comprehensive workflow to build a healthcare system with artificial intelligence. More exactly an intelligent system that can detect and diagnose skin cancer. While most work that use deep learning techniques focuses either on detection or diagnosis skin cancer, we have use these techniques to develope a model that does both tasks at once. Transfer learning was applied on different models of object detection and diagnosis using a dataset from Kaggle with TensorFlow API. The dataset images are a total set of 3297 dermatoscopic images. To train our model, 2637 images were used. And to test it, 660 images were used. VGG16 was used as an object recognition backbone network (for diagnosis) and Yolo as the object detection framework. The evaluation accuracy of the model was more than 83 %, which is promising.

articleTitle: Unlocking Enhanced Bandwidth for 5G Microstrip Antennas: A Comparative Analysis of Substrate Anisotropy and Thickness Manipulation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This research paper investigates the resonant frequency and bandwidth characteristics of a microstrip patch antenna tailored for 5G applications. The study focuses on two key factors that can impact antenna performance, substrate thickness and uniaxial electric anisotropy ratio (AR). Through a comprehensive analysis, we demonstrate that augmenting the substrate thickness and increasing the AR ratio yield notable enhancements in antenna bandwidth. Moreover, fine-tuning the AR ratio is found to amplify the operating frequency without introducing undesirable drawbacks associated with increasing substrate thickness. These findings offer valuable insights into optimizing microstrip patch antennas for 5G applications, paving the way for improved wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of LSTM, GRU, and MLP Neural Networks for Short-Term Solar Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Renewable energies, including solar energy, have gained significant importance in the global energy landscape as a sustainable and eco-friendly alternative to fossil fuels. Solar energy, harnessed from solar radiation and meteorological factors, plays a crucial role in power grids worldwide. Improving energy output forecasts is essential for efficient planning and optimization of solar energy generation in the future.The primary objective of this research was to create and assess three distinct neural networks, namely Long-Short-Term-Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) for predicting the power generation of PV solar system. The training data was sourced from Adrar City, Algeria, covering the period from 2016 to 2020. The examination of these algorithms' performance revealed that LSTM neural network outperformed both GRU and MLP models. This can be attributed to LSTM's adeptness in managing time-series data, which significantly enhanced its ability to accurately forecast solar power production.

articleTitle: Comparison between the incremental conductivity and grey-wolf method for MPPT in photovoltaic system under irregular shadow conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Shade significantly reduces the efficiency of a photovoltaic (PV) system, resulting in power loss and lower output. Energy from solar panels can be maximized by using MPPT algorithms to maximize power points, minimize shading's negative effects, and enhance power collection. This article compares two MPPT techniques, Incremental Conductivity (INC) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO), under shaded conditions with uniform and uneven irradiance and temperature variation. To demonstrate the practical application of MPPT techniques, a configuration of photovoltaic panels connected in a series under shade is described. In addition, the study examines the effectiveness of these algorithms in maintaining accurate maximum power point tracking as well as their adaptability to changing environmental conditions. Based on the results of our study, it can be concluded that the GWO algorithm outperforms the INC algorithm in precisely tracking the maximum power point over a diverse range of environmental variables, such as shadow, irradiance, and temperature, among others.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Low Voltage Electrical Network Pollution Using a Two-Level PAPF Controlled by the ANN-PQ Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The study focuses on enhancing the performance of APFs (the two-level parallel active power filter (PAPF)) by investigating the efficiency of the ANN-PQ algorithm in comparison to the conventional PQ algorithm. The proposed ANN-PQ algorithm leverages the capabilities of artificial neural networks to optimize harmonic cancellation and reactive power compensation, thereby improving power quality. Results of simulation are presented to showcase the effectiveness of the two algorithms in mitigating harmonic distortion, reducing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), and enhancing current waveform quality. Through a comprehensive analysis of key parameters such as THD reduction, power factor improvement, and load current quality, the study provides a detailed evaluation of the effectiveness of the ANN-PQ algorithm compared to the conventional PQ algorithm.

articleTitle: Control of Water Pumping System Based On Floating Photovoltaic System with a Solar Tracking Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents a solar tracking control of a floating photovoltaic system using a submerged water pumping system. Addressing the issues of limited space and overall efficiency represents a significant challenge in the realm of renewable energy, particularly in the context of photovoltaic systems. The floating solar tracking system offers a viable solution to enhance both surface and efficiency. To feed efficiently the system where the light intensity is higher and energy is in the form of Direct Current, tracking is the alignment of the solar panel so that it is always perpendicular to the sun beams. Thus, this work is divided into two parts; Based on submerged pumping systems, the floating solar tracking system is modeled and controlled. The practical application of our work’s experimental model is covered in the second section. The use of a photovoltaic panel coupled to a DC-DC Boost converter powering the two submerged pumps allowed us to implement the concept of floating solar panels with the pumping solar tracker. To indicate the direction of sun radiation, these pumps are coupled to the L298d circuit and controlled by an Arduino mega.

articleTitle: Comparative Study betwenn P&O, IncCond and MSC algorithmes for MPPT Control of PV systeme
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: PV energy is a valuable source, however devices must be operated at its MPP to maximum efficiency. The complexity of this task arises from the nonlinearity exhibited by the current-voltage characteristics of photovoltaic systems, which is impacted by factors such as temperature and radiance conditions.The aim of this investigation is to assess the efficacy of a SMC-based MPPT technique for a boost-type DC/DC converter. The focus is on assessing the ability of this technique to maintain stability and optimal performance in the face of rapidly changing sun radiances. The resilience of the controller is evaluated by comparing it with the P&O approach and IncCond method. This evaluation is conducted using Matlab/Simulink to model the PV-MPPT system.

Author Keywords: Sliding mode control based MPPT techniques

articleTitle: Optimization of distributed generations within radial distribution systems to enhance system performance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The increasing electricity consumption across various residential, commercial and industrial sectors has led to the incorporation of renewable energies based Distributed Generations (DGs) to satisfy electrical demand and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. Meanwhile, appropriate integration of DGs in Radial Distribution Systems (RDS) is a significant factor in improving system performance. This paper suggests an Adaptive Particle Swarm Optimization (APSO) algorithm to identify the optimal size, position and power factor (PF) of DG units to reduce total real power losses and improve the voltage profile of the whole system while satisfying the operational constraints. Two DG types were considered: the first operates at unity PF and the second at optimum PF. The study concluded that the operation of DGs at their optimum PF is more impactful in reducing power losses and improving the voltage profile in the RDS. The efficacy of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated via simulation conducted on an IEEE 69-bus distribution system, and the obtained results corresponded with those found in the existing literature.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Hybrid Energy Storage Systems for Remote Standalone Renewable Energy Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The increasing demand for reliable and sustainable energy sources has led to significant advancements in the field of hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) for remote stand-alone power plants. These power plants, located in off-grid and isolated areas, face unique challenges due to their distance from conventional energy infrastructure. As a result, researchers and engineers have been actively pursuing innovative solutions that combine multiple energy storage technologies to ensure continuous and efficient power supply. This abstract highlights the recent progress in the development of hybrid energy storage systems tailored for remote stand-alone power plants. The integration of diverse energy storage technologies, such as batteries, supercapacitors, and flywheels, has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing the intermittency of renewable energy sources in remote locations. Recent advancements have focused on optimizing the operation and control strategies of HESS to maximize energy utilization, minimize storage losses, and extend system lifespan. Advanced control algorithms, including model predictive control (MPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, have been applied to manage the charge and discharge cycles of different storage components effectively.

articleTitle: Impact of Fuel Cell System Technologies on the Design of UAVs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The use of multi-rotor UAVs in various industries is becoming increasingly popular, and the implementation of utilizing fuel cell technology for power has been recognized as a strategy to improve flight times beyond what is currently possible with lithium batteries. This paper proposes a study of the influence of fuel cell system technologies on the design of UAVs by focusing on the reduction of the total fuel cell weight, the propulsion power, fuel consumption and endurance, this might improve the efficiency of drones. For this study, an X8 multirotor drone powered by proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cell power module with a maximum total weight of 25 kg has been selected as a case study. In addition, a different types of fuel cells equipped with a 7.2 L hydrogen tank pressurized to 300 bar are analyzed and evaluated to improve their characteristics and to determine the most suitable option for the UAV. Based on the results, the optimal fuel cell technology for powering the UAV is identified and it stands out among the various options evaluated. The Aerostak 2000 fuel cell is the selected option among these technologies due to its higher performance properties. Overall, the development and advancement of fuel cell technology significantly affects the performance and capabilities of UAVs.

articleTitle: Children Autism Detection Using Residual CNN and EfficientNetB1
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Autism is a developmental disorder that can cause serious social, communication, and behavioral issues. Early intervention for autistic children can aid in improving cognitive ability and reducing autistic symptoms. In this study, we investigate how well Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models perform when estimating automated engagement from autistic children's faces. The main contribution is to create a CNN residual using residual blocks containing Depthwise convolution layers (DCL) and convolution layers to reduce the number of parameters in the model by treating each channel of the input image separately with a Depthwise kernel. A Residual CNN model and EfficientNetB1 have been proposed for autism image classification. The EfficientNetB1 architecture with Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer is used for scaling dimensions, and a classification layer is done with a SoftMax layer. The Kaggle dataset, which contains 2,940 images of faces, is used in the experiments. The model's performance was evaluated and compared to existing models in terms of precision, recall, f1-score, and overall accuracy. The two models used achieved classification rates of 86.33% and 88%, respectively, for Residual CNN and EfficientNetB1. According to the results, the method outperforms others using the same dataset.

articleTitle: An efficient Neural Network Approach for Perovskite Materials Band Gap Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In our study, we harnessed the potential of Artificial Neural Networks, specifically the Multilayer Perceptron, to forecast the band gap of Perovskite Materials. Our model demonstrated remarkable generalization capabilities, achieving a mean square error of just 0.002 when applied to new materials. The key descriptors utilized in our analysis included the elemental composition of each site within the perovskite material and any associated doping compounds. To gain deeper insights, we further explored the impact of each descriptor on the band gap through Pearson's correlation matrix analysis. This approach not only provides an efficient means for estimating Band Gap values but also simplifies the prediction process, offering a powerful tool for materials science research.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Real-Time Hand Landmark Recognition with MediaPipe for R12 Robot Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In the evolving world of robotics, the way humans and robots interact plays a crucial role in the overall system performance and user experience. Traditionally, robotic control for accomplishing tasks have been dominated by programming languages like ROBOFORTH or touchpad interfaces. However, these methods often create barriers to user interaction. This study explores the potential of hand gesture recognition, specifically focusing on the deep-learning MediaPipe library’s real-time hand-landmark detection capabilities. We present a system that combines MediaPipes abilities with controlling the ST Robotics R12 robot, allowing real-time hand gestures to be translated into robotic drawing actions and tasks. This integration offers a natural and interactive communication medium that could revolutionize how humans carry out tasks with robots. By leveraging MediaPipes computer vision and deep learning techniques, we successfully controlled the R12 robot through gesture-based interactions. The system effectively translated hand gestures into robotic drawing functions and specific tasks such as object relocation. However, future improvements should concentrate on enhancing precision, reevaluating reliance on ROBOFORTH and exploring MATLAB Simulink’s potential for advanced gesture-based control algorithms.

articleTitle: Poincaré map Identification of Switched Nonlinear Systems Using SINDy Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents an extended approach for the identification and characterization of limit cycles in switched nonlinear dynamical systems using the Poincaré map and the Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) technique. We can effectively unravel critical insights from the complex behavior exhibited by switched nonlinear systems. This extended technique of Poincaré map identification using the SINDy method allows us to comprehensively comprehend the system’s evolution during mode transitions across specific intersections. The proposed method plays a pivotal role in both stabilizing switched systems and conducting a comprehensive analysis of their limit cycles. Indeed, the precise identification of Poincaré maps enables exploration of the system stability and its periodicity patterns, offering invaluable tools for controlling switched nonlinear systems. These insights hold significant promise for making well-informed decisions across a wide range of practical applications.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Reconfiguration Based on Hourly Load Variation Via New Optimization Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper proposes applying Equilibrium Optimizer (EO), African Vultures (AVOA), and Gorilla Troops (GTO), recently developed optimization techniques, to find the optimal reconfiguration of the electrical distribution network that reduces the annual cost of energy losses incurred during the network's permanent operation, considering the hourly variations of load demand. First, we suggest a mathematical formulation of the objective function and of all the necessary operational and radiality constraints that must be met. These algorithms are then implemented on the 69-node test system for analysis and resolution purposes. Finally, the efficacy of the suggested methods is evaluated. Results show that using the EO algorithm has a substantial impact on reducing the costs related to annual energy loss and improving the node voltage levels.

articleTitle: Investigation of a Photovoltaic Immersed Water Pumping System: Theoretical and Experimental Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This research conducts a theoretical and practical study of a photovoltaic system for submerged water pumping, including a PV generator, DC/DC converter, PMDC motor, and a centrifugal pump. It assesses performance using MPPT with the P&O algorithm in Matlab/Simulink, accounting for HMT and weather effects on flow rate. A dSPACE1104 was used to validate the simulation results in data acquisition and control system design.

articleTitle: Enhancing Dental Caries Classification Through A VGG16-Based Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Dental caries is a common oral disease of global concern and early diagnosis is essential to prevent it. In this paper, we use deep learning to develop a dental radiography diagnostic support system. The aim is to classify dental images as caries or healthy. We transfer learning the pre-trained VGG16 model, to classify our data. This smart way to use pre-trained VGG16 saves time and resources. To implement our system, we created a dataset of periapical dental radiography images, collected in a group dental practice, and then enlarged using the data augmentation processes. The accuracy of the proposed model is 99%.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study Between EMD-MCKD and EMD-MEDA Techniques for the Bearing Faults Diagnosis in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The significance of induction motors has been greatly heightened due to the rapid advancements in modern industrial production. Therefore, a fault diagnosis based on vibration signals is therefore critical in industry and academia. In this context, we compared Empirical Mode Decomposition combined with Maximum Correlation Kurtosis Deconvolution (EMD-MCKD) to EMD with Minimum Entropy Deconvolution Adjusted (EMD-MEDA). In order to improve fault diagnosis, we apply to the reconstructed signal the technique of Maximum Correlation Kurtosis Deconvolution (MCKD). Simultaneously, subjected to Minimum Entropy Deconvolution Adjusted (MEDA). Finally, the outcomes are comprehensively analyzed and compared to identify the optimal technique for diagnosing bearing faults. This study is based upon experimental findings, and demonstrates the effectiveness and suitability of the EMD-MEDA technique, clearly promising in bearing fault diagnosis and extract the characteristics of the fault in the signal, by evaluating its accuracy and comparing its performance to EMD-MCKD.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network MPPT Based Lead Acid Battery Charge Controller for Isolated Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The renewable energy sector has become one of the fastest growing. However, the price of a kWh from renewable resources is too expensive compared to energy produced from fossil sources. For this reason, maximising production plays an important role in relation to the cost price of energy. To this end, this paper proposes an ANN MPPT control for a PV system, together with a lead acid battery controller. The results obtained show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach to Estimate Ultraviolet Irradiance from Solar Radiation Data
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: One primary cause of degradation for materials exposed to the outdoors is ultraviolet (UV) light. To estimate their rate of degradation and determine their longevity (service life), truthful quantification of the UV irradiation incident on their surfaces is needed. In this paper, several neural models are proposed to estimate three UV components based on the broadband global horizontal irradiance and various atmospheric constituents. Using spectral results obtained with the SMARTS model for a large variety of atmospheric conditions and sun positions, three groups of experiments are carried out: the first one is designed to estimate the total UV irradiance at the surface (280–400 nm), whereas the second and third groups aim at estimating its UV-A and UV-B fractions, respectively. The results generally show a good prediction performance, particularly for the first two groups.

articleTitle: Security Performance Optimization of Aerial Downlink NOMA-IRS Aided Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Advancements in next-generation wireless networks are being driven by the introduction of innovative technologies, a focus of numerous research studies. Consequently, the Intelligent Reflective Surface (IRS) within Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) networks has emerged as a valuable and favorable technology for this purpose. In this paper, we delve into the security challenges of an aerial downlink in IRS-aided NOMA networks, especially when faced with potential eavesdropping. We further explore an optimization strategy for secrecy performance, utilizing the Multi-Objective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm.

articleTitle: PMSM Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis using EKF Observer and FFT for Sensorless Input-Output Linearization Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This research focuses on the inter-turn short circuit fault detection of the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) using the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) observer as a linearization control without sensors. The Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is utilized for the spectral analysis of electrical and mechanical properties during the fault diagnosis step of the fault detection procedure, which includes variations in the stator resistance estimation by the EKF observer. The efficiency of sensorless control and fault detection techniques is illustrated through a simulation in the MATLAB/Simulink environment.

articleTitle: Power management control of a Photovoltaic Power System with Batteries and Fuel Cells in Stand Alone Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Renewable energy sources exhibit significant variability in their power output, making it necessary to incorporate a storage system. Batteries, and fuel cells, are the most used storage in photovoltaic systems. These technologies efficiently store surplus renewable energy for utilization during periods of low generation. However, batteries have a limitation in their lifetime, which is affected by the deterioration of their state of charge. Additionally, fuel cells' performance can be influenced by the hydrogen consumption rate. The supervision of a photovoltaic system with storage or multiple storage units involves multi-objective control. It not only allows for power regulation and optimization but also ensures a maximum state of charge for batteries and minimal hydrogen consumption for fuel cells. This paper considers and compares various scenarios of PV with storage to identify the optimal solution for specific applications, such as on-grid, off-grid, or electric vehicle setups. Simulation results are presented to support the findings.

articleTitle: A linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control based PSO to control Twin Rotor MIMO System with experimental validation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This study presents a strategy known as Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) as a means to mitigate the effects of unidentified interior and/or external perturbations on nonlinear systems. In our approach, we have chosen to utilize a Twin Rotor Multi-Input Multi-Output (TRMS) helicopter simulator. The utilization of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) method was employed in the synthesis of coefficients for the Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) approach. The findings indicate that the TRMS nonlinear system exhibits effective disturbance rejection capabilities, as demonstrated in both simulated and real-world scenarios. The outcomes of a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) control system that has been enhanced using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) are also contrasted with those generated using the suggested methodology.

articleTitle: Comparison of Single - Phase-Shift And Extended -phase -shift Modulation of Isolated Bidirectional DC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: To ameliorate the chracterisation of isolated bidirectional Dual-Active-Bridge DC–DC (IBCD), various modulation methods are present . two control methods , single phase-shift control (SPS), extended phase shift (EPS) are research and compared for a full-bridge-based isolated bidirectional dc–dc converter , analysis of operation mode and demonstrating mathematical models of transmission power, backflow power, and current stress. finally , simulation results confirm the correct performance of EPS control.

articleTitle: Improving classification accuracy for motor imagery BCI using DWT based Features
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) act as vital bridges connecting human brains to external devices. They help people with disabilities do things on their own, like tasks and talking to others. One of the challenges of the BCI motor imagery electroencephalography (MI-EEG) based is the low accuracy of the imagined movements recognition. This paper introduces new features based on the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to make MI-EEG signal decoding more accurate. Our system utilizes 18 features extracted from both the time and the frequency domains to feed a pre-trained classifier in order to identify hand movement. Many classifiers were used in this study namely the support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression (LR), k-nearest neighbors (KNN), and linear discriminant analysis (LDA). The effectiveness of the proposed system was evaluated based on the classification accuracy (CA) using the BCI Competition II Dataset III. The results of our experiments demonstrate that the LR classifier outperforms all studied classifiers achieving an impressive CA of 92.14% while using the LR classifier with just 6 features selected by genetic algorithm optimization (GA).

articleTitle: Allocation resource using new intelligent algorithm: discrete particle swarm optimization (DPSO)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The allocation of radio resources is one of the greatest challenges facing mobile operators, as they have to respond to a dizzying demand for wireless multimedia services, and exponentially growing data traffic, hence the emergence of a new generation of mobile cellular networks. In this paper, we address the allocation problem in a 5G cell using Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) transmission technique and propose a new allocation strategy using a discrete particle swarm optimization (DPSO) intelligence method. The aim is to guarantee an optimal distribution of resources between users, whatever their positions, so as to maximize a utility function. Simulation results show that the performance of the proposed intelligent discrete particle swarm optimization (DPSO) algorithm achieves very good inter-user performance compared with the standard particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm in terms of throughput, spectral and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Hardware in the Loop Simulation Architecture for Quadrotor UAV
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper introduces a comprehensive Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) architecture for a quadrotor helicopter. This architecture also incorporates Man-in-the-Loop capabilities, allowing for dynamic testing of embedded control systems and pilot training in realistic flight scenarios. The architectural design is tailored to integrate with real UAV systems seamlessly.

articleTitle: Decoupled Unknown-Input Observer for Takagi-Sugeno Systems: Application to Three Phase Interleaved Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents the application of a Takagi-Sugeno based Decoupled Unknown-Input Observer for Three-Phase Interleaved Boost Converters for fuel cell applications. Harnessing the potential of a single sensor, the proposed methodology efficiently estimates all the remaining system states and the unknown input. This unique implementation of the Decoupled Unknown-Input Observer in the Interleaved Boost Converters ensures precise state estimation while effectively addressing system nonlinearities. Moreover, an observer based controller is implemented to regulate the DC-bus voltage converter, and its performance is confirmed through simulation test. The proposed work promises to enhance the reliability and cost-effectiveness of power conversion systems.

articleTitle: An Optimization Technique for Improving Parameters of the Inverse Jiles-Atherton Hysteresis Formulation in Case of Steel Sheet Fe3%Si
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In a current study, we present an innovative model for optimization of hysteresis cycle parameters. Proposed model is applied to a steel sheet. In doing so, we have defined the interest of the use of Jiles-Atherton phenomenological model and we have specified our study on the case of the inverse model. The exploit of Particle Swarm Optimization technique was discussed with details. B(H) curves produced by modeling and experimentation are shown for the quasi-static frequency under sinusoidal magnetic excitation applied to a GNO Fe3%Si steel sheet. Simulation results are analyzed and compared with experimental obtained B(H) curve. In a first situation, a study was conducted after optimization, while in the second one; the specified investigation was carried out with optimization. The simulated and optimized B(H) curve and the experimental data show and confirm an excellent agreement. A highly successful performance has been made, validating our proposed Model.

articleTitle: Improvement of energy management of standalone hybrid generation power system using Adaptive neuro fuzzy system
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: An intelligent energy management of a standalone hybrid generating power system is shown in this study. In this work, we compare traditional energy management systems (EMS) with modern intelligence methodologies (The Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) and the Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC).) for controlling battery charging and discharging, determining load priority, and secondary charge management. The hybrid system is made up of photovoltaic (PV) panels, wind turbines, and energy storage. A DC-DC power converter connects all energy sources to DC bus. The comprehensive system is depicted through a dynamic and steady-state mathematical model, along with simulation studies. MATLAB (Simulink) environment is used to construct this model.

articleTitle: Influence of Short-Circuit Arc Resistance on Distance Protection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The presence of fault resistance can introduce inaccuracies in estimating the fault distance within a transmission line, potentially leading to unreliable performance of a distance relay. In this study, overhead transmission lines are a critical component of power systems and represent the most cost-effective means of transmitting electricity from remote sources of generation to the end customer. Therefore, it is crucial to protect and maintain them in service to ensure a secure power supply for end-users and safeguard the capital investments of power companies. Arcing faults are a common occurrence in power systems, and understanding the effects of fault arcs is essential for power system protection. Numerical algorithms can be developed to analyze and pinpoint the position of arc faults in power systems. The aim of this research is to develop a model of arcing faults and investigate their impact on distance protection.

articleTitle: Adaptive Observer-Based Synchronization For a Class of Fractional-Order Nonlinear Systems Subject to Unknown Inputs
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The synchronization of a fractional-order drive-response configuration system is addressed in this study. A slave fractional order adaptive observer system is designed in order to synchronize with a particular master fractional chaotic system whose dynamical model is exposed to unknown inputs data. Based on the stability theorem of Lyapunov, a fractional-order adaptation law is derived to estimate the unknown inputs,the observation and estimation errors stability is analyzed. To validate the benefits of the novel synchronization approach an application example to fractional-order Chua system is presented.

articleTitle: Parameters Identification of Induction Motor Based on The Equilibrium Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this research paper, the parameters of the induction motor (IM) were identified using equilibrium optimizer (EO) which is a modern algorithm that appeared most recently in farmarzi and al’s work and was applied in different researches fields, the results obtiened shows that they are very close to the real parameters. In order to verify the efficiancy and accuracy of the EO algorithm among the other metaheuristics methods the results of IM parameters obtained with the EO were compared with those obtained with particle swarm optimisation algorithm PSO along the iterations. It will be revealed in this work also, that the identified parameters obtained with EO have an advantage in improving the accuracy of their values with the speed of convergence of the objective function of EO for the identification of IM parameters compared to that obtained from PSO.

articleTitle: Improved-GWO for Shunt Capacitors Placements and Dimensions in Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Distribution system operators continually grapple with the challenge of minimizing Total Line Losses (TLLs). In response, our research integrates Shunt Capacitors (ShCs) and deploys the Improved Grey Wolf Optimizer (I-GWO) algorithm to determine the optimal sizing and placement of these capacitors. The analysis is conducted considering multiple constraints, such as line limitations, load point voltage levels, and prescribed capacitor thresholds. The approach is evaluated on IEEE distribution systems with 10, 15, 85, and 118 buses, ensuring a realistic assessment. Our results underscore the superior performance of the proposed algorithm when compared to existing literature, offering an effective solution for reducing losses in electric networks.

articleTitle: A Permittivity-Sensitive Sensor with a Sensing Area based on a Resonator with Two Legs Stretched Inwards
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this work, an antenna-based sensor is proposed to monitor permittivity variation. On FR4 epoxy of 12x12x1.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, our structure was designed, and then validated on HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator) software and CST (Computer Simulation Technology). The feed line of antenna and the sensor detection zone were etched on the top and bottom of the substrate, respectively. To distribute the maximum E-field in the detection zone, a slot based on resonator with two legs stretched inwards (RTLSI) was introduced on the ground plane of our antenna. To test the sensor’s sensitivity, MUTS (Material Under Test) were putted alternatively on the RTLSI slot. The sensor’s sensitivity was estimated by a polynomial of third degree. This sensor is able to detect a relative permittivity variation with sensitivity equal to 1.2 to 6.3 times the sensitivity of sensors presented in previous works; in addition, the size of sensor was reduced.
