articleTitle: PID controller using new GWO strategy to drive dual star induction motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This work deals with optimizing the parameters of the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller to improve the speed control performance of (DSIM) driven by field-oriented indirect control IFOC. The strategy used is a promising gray wolf optimization (GWO) algorithm based on artificial intelligence techniques. Compared to using the PID controller alone, the technique provided is more effective in improving the stability of the speed loop response. The simulation results under Matlab environment demonstrate that the designed PID-GWO speed controller achieves good dynamic behavior of DSIM, perfect speed tracking without overshoot, better performance and high robustness.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Silicon Carbide MOSFET Inverter for Electric Vehicle Traction Applications using Python
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents the design and simulation of a Silicon Carbide (Sic) MOSFET inverter for an electric vehicle (EV) using Python, the study focuses on simulating the behavior of a Permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) using Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM) to control the speed of the motor and the influence of DC and AC filter on the weight, the Mass and the efficiency of the inverter. the use of SiC MOSFETs in the inverter aims to enhance performance and efficiency by achieving higher switching frequencies .The findings of this study contribute to the understanding and optimization of SiC MOSFET-based inverters for EV traction and an enrichment to the open source community of specialized Python library developers. Thereby advancing the development of efficient electric propulsion technologies for sustainable transportation

articleTitle: Current sensor fault tolerant control of a double star induction motor DSIM using fuzzy sliding control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this article, we proposed a sliding fuzzy control for a double star induction machine DSIM to improve an adaptive control even in case of a presence of a sudden defect in the machine. to ensure maximum energy efficiency and continuity of service a fault tolerant control is integrated to to detect, isolate, and reconfigure the controller by comparing the measured and the required value of the stator current in this paper we presented a current sensor fault which is a common defect in the induction machine and also to verify and confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method . Simulation results are tested in matlab / simulink environment.

articleTitle: An Artificial Intelligence-Based System for Detecting Diseases in Apple Tree Branches
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This research focuses on the detection of diseases on apple tree branches using artificial intelligence (AI). The aim of this study is to develop an intelligent system that can automatically detect and segment diseases on apple tree branches based on image analysis. Traditional manual detection methods are time-consuming, costly, and prone to human errors. By leveraging advancements in machine learning, image processing, and deep learning algorithms, an AI-based system can provide accurate and real-time information about the health status of apple trees, enabling farmers to take preventive measures and optimize their crop production. The proposed system combines machine learning techniques with image analysis and data processing to assist farmers in maintaining the health of their trees and reducing crop losses. This work presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of the system, demonstrating its effectiveness in disease detection on apple tree branches.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Direct Torque Control Validation of Induction Machine by FPGA Hardware Co-simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: this work describes the development, implementation and validation of hardware architecture on FPGA for fuzzy DTC control of induction motor. This approach enables addressing the primary challenges associated with this control technique, which include mitigating torque ripples, minimizing flux fluctuations, and achieving precise switching frequency control. The introduction of this method has sparked numerous research endeavors aimed at demonstrating its effectiveness and resolving its inherent limitations. Specifically, this study focuses on validating a fuzzy DTC implementation hardware on the development card ML402, which utilizes an FPGA circuit of the Xilinx Virtex-4 type. This validation is carried out using Xilinx system generator and VHDL description language. The results obtained show the effectiveness of the proposed approach for controlling the induction machine and reducing flux and torque ripples.

articleTitle: Power Flow Optimization of the Adrar Power System in Algeria Using the Whale Optimizer Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The (WOA) whale optimization algorithm is a highly effective method used to find global solutions to complex problems. The purpose of this project is to apply WOA method on the Adrar power system with (WPG) wind power generation in order to solve the (OPF) optimal power flow dispatch, reducing emission cost and fuel cost minimization. Arguably, using this algorithm can help improve the efficiency and performance of energy systems and improve environmental performance by improving power flow in the power system, as well as fuel costs and emissions. The results obtained from this study offer valuable insights into the efficacy of the WOA algorithm in enhancing the Adrar power system while effectively attaining the desired objectives.

articleTitle: Direct Torque Control of Sensorless Two FPIM Parallel Connected Using Slide Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Direct torque control DTC provides decoupled electromagnetic torque and stator flux control for high-performance AC drives. Nevertheless, this technique relies on accurate knowledge of the stator flux module and position, mainly during low-speed regions. Therefore, a sliding mode sensorless stator flux and speed DTC for two five-phase induction motors FPIM connected in parallel is discussed. The implemented slide mode observer SMO offers a robust estimation and control of the FPIM based primarily on measured variables (stator voltages and currents), eliminating the need for flux and speed sensors that reduce system reliability. The present results verify and compare the proposed and conventional schemes’ performance, effectiveness, and feasibility.

articleTitle: Real-Time Backstepping Control Based MRAS Speed Estimation of an Induction Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This work presents a real-time evaluation of a sensorless MRAS-backstepping control applied to an induction process (IM). To run the system in safe mode, a backstepping method is first implemented. It guarantees decoupled torque and flux management of the IM without the need for an additional regulator by removing the proportional/integral controller (PI) and decreasing the number of gains that are highly reliant on the temperature-dependent IM parameters. The backstepping control is designed to attain the required speed and flux, and it is ideally suited for regulating an uncertain system that may be affected by external disturbances. Its formulation is based on the application of Lyapunov functions to assure the overall stability of the system. The second section presents a model reference adaptive system (MRAS) to estimate rotor speed and eliminate the sensor, the system's weakest link. Utilizing dSPACE 1104 cards, the suggested control procedure is evaluated. The achieved experimental results indicate that the entire system runs smoothly, with the proposed MRAS-backstepping providing high performance, the system successfully tracking the speed profile under tolerable load, and the system maintaining its dynamic behavior at different speed levels.

articleTitle: A Stable and Admissible Explicit Solution to Fuzzy Predictive Control using polyhedral invariant sets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: One of the main problems in Model Predictive control MPC is the lack of guaranteed feasibility and stability. In this paper we propose a strategy to resolve the optimization problem associated with fuzzy predictive control to find a solution that is both stable and admissible. The proposed explicit approach, combined with the theory of invariant sets, provides a secure and admissible solution for the optimization problem. The approach begins by applying the principles of decision making in a fuzzy environment, specifically the Bellman Zadeh approach. Next, we divide the state space into separate regions the objective of this separation is to identify the state region that contains the appropriate solutions. We start with the terminal region and then working down, developing a set of permissible control laws for each region. The simulation results confirm that our strategy effectively addresses the problems of feasibility and stability in Model Predictive Control.

articleTitle: Effect of the applied high voltage on the neutralization efficiency of negative charges accumulated on polypropylene film surface
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this study, experimental characterizations obtained by non-contact measurements of the profile and decay of the surface potential have been carried out. The experiments were performed on polypropylene (PP) films (50 mm × 25 mm). The samples were charged for duration of 5 seconds in ambient air of temperature and relative humidity, using a negative polarity dc corona triode electrode system (needle-grid-plate configuration). The study investigates the impact of the charging voltage on the surface potential profile and decay, with varying values of the grid voltage. The accumulated charges on the samples surface were neutralized by a sinusoidal alternating corona discharge generated at power frequency of 50 Hz. This neutralization process was performed after the charging procedure, where the samples move within the ac corona discharge zone. The effect of the applied high voltage on the neutralization of electric charges was studied. The evaluation of neutralization efficiency was evaluated by the comparison of surface electric potential profiles before and after neutralization in a static mode. The experimental results obtained indicate that higher applied high voltage induces better neutralization efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Egg Packing SCARA Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The considerable technological progress currently taking place in the world has resulted in a rapid boom of robotics in industry, as in all other sectors. Considering also the economic constraint, the reduction of product prices is a first necessity. It is against this backdrop that this paper proposes the design of a low-cost SCARA robot and the adoption of its end unit for packing eggs. First, the design of the robot is presented, followed by an optimisation analysis aims to perform egg packing while ensure a high productivity and low power consumption to ensuring the completeness of final price of eggs. The results obtained show the productivity of the robot depending on its simple design and relatively low cost.

articleTitle: Estimating Energy Parameters for Photovoltaic Modules Using Mathematical Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The aim of this study is to evaluate three different models for predicting the energy output of a photovoltaic (PV) module situated at the Applied Research Unit in Renewable Energy (URAER) within Algeria. The electrical energy generated by the PV module was monitored using a DC regulator designed to maximize electrical power extraction from the module. Simultaneously, various meteorological parameters, including solar irradiation and air temperature, were recorded using a Kipp & ZonenTM CMP21 pyranometer and a Pt-100 temperature sensor, respectively. The PV module under investigation is composed of polycrystalline silicon (poly-Si) and was observed during the period year. The simulation outcomes exhibit a high level of agreement with the empirical measurements. Notably, the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) for these models exceeds 0.8975, indicating strong alignment between the measured data and the linear model employed.

articleTitle: Optimizing Corona Ring Design for 400 kV Cap-Pin String Insulator to Minimize Surface Electric Field under Various Surface Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to reduce the electric field stress along the surface of the 400 kV cap-pin string insulator by optimizing its corona ring design. The cap-pin string insulator, composed of glass material and consisting of 1512 L units, is designed and investigated within a 2D-axisymmetric environment using COMSOL software. Firstly, we optimize the corona ring’s radius, tube radius, and height. Secondly, the corona ring shape is optimized to more effectively decrease the surface electric field, despite the resulting increase in its weight. Finally, the optimized shape is replaced by multiple corona rings, each with a small radius, positioned in the most deformed area, to enhance the insulator’s performance in terms of both surface electric field and corona ring weight. The COBYLA algorithm is utilized as the optimization method throughout the study. This research examines clean, uniformly polluted, and Room Temperature Vulcanizing (RTV) silicon rubber-coated surface conditions. The obtained results are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Accurate and Dynamic Environment Modeling: Cost-effective Alternatives to 3D LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The reconstruction of dynamic environments is indispensable in numerous applications, including robotics, ensuring autonomous vehicle safety, industrial surveillance, and environment modeling and mapping. The utilization of LiDAR 3D technology is widespread due to its ability to provide precise measurements of distance and angles. However, due to its prohibitive cost, the widespread accessibility of 3D LiDAR remains limited. In this paper, we propose a low-cost alternative to 3D LiDAR technology that utilizes readily available components, namely the RPLidar A1 and a simple servo motor, both controlled by a Raspberry Pi3 and programmed using Python. The innovative approach proposed in this paper successfully achieved highly accurate environment representations in 3D. These reconstructions can be utilized for surface mapping, scene classification, and facilitating typical robotic tasks such as autonomous navigation and collision avoidance.

articleTitle: A Control grid-connected PV system with NPC Multi-level inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper introduces a control strategy for a distributed generation system utilizing photovoltaics. The system employs a dual-stage configuration consisting of a DC-DC boost converter and a five-level neutral-point-clamped (NPC) voltage source inverter (VSI). In order to control the inverter and the current injected into the grid, the voltage-oriented control (VOC) approach and pulse width modulation (PWM) technology are utilized. The voltage-oriented control approach guarantees effective power monitoring, voltage balancing, NPC inverter functionality, and the injection of clean sinusoidal grid current, even in the face of potential dynamic variations. The effectiveness of the proposed control scheme is demonstrated using MATLAB/Simulink simulations of the electric power distribution system's steady-state and transient responses.

articleTitle: Tasks Offloading Techniques in the Era of Mobile Augmented Reality for Sparse and Dense Mist Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Mobile Augmented Reality (MAR) has witnessed substantial growth, yet challenges like task delay, bandwidth constraints, and device energy drain persist. The emergence of edge and mist computing offers a remedy. This paper investigates MAR within mist computing, evaluating it across sparse and dense environments using four task orchestration algorithms. We assess CPU usage, mist layer and WiFi energy consumption, task execution time, and network utilization. Our study demonstrates the advantages of mist-enabled task orchestration, showcasing improved MAR system performance. This research contributes insights into the symbiotic relationship between MAR and mist computing, highlighting mist’s potential to enhance MAR challenges. The findings underscore mist computing’s viability in advancing MAR applications and systems.

articleTitle: Design and Control of PV Emulator based on DC-DC Push-Pull Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to design and control a photovoltaic emulator (PVE). The latter is controlled using PI controller in order to force the DC-DC push-pull converter trajectory to track the PV panel model reference. To achieve the objective of this work, a mathematical model of the PV panel is presented and analyzed. This model is obtained from the PV panel’s equivalent electrical circuit. Then, we discussed the performance of the system in open loop and defined PI parameters upon that. The controller design is achieved in through frequency analysis (Bode diagram). The founded results show the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed photovoltaic emulator.

articleTitle: Enhanced Fingerprint Image Compression using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to fingerprint compression using the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm. The goal is to achieve high compression ratios while maintaining image quality. The DDPG algorithm combines deep neural networks with reinforcement learning and is well-suited for complex control tasks. Experimental evaluations are conducted on a benchmark fingerprint dataset, comparing the proposed method with state-of-the-art compression techniques. Results show that the DDPG-based compression approach achieves competitive compression ratios while preserving important fingerprint details. The algorithm demonstrates robustness across diverse fingerprint samples. Computational efficiency is also evaluated, considering training and compression times. The findings indicate a balanced trade-off between complexity and performance, making the DDPG-based approach suitable for practical fingerprint compression applications.

articleTitle: 12/8 Switched Reluctance Machine Modeling and Analysis Based on Finte Elements Method in the Presence of the no-Linearity effects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The primary objective of this research paper is to investigate and analyze the nonlinear phenomena observed in a 12/8 switched reluctance machine (SRM). The machine demonstrates significant nonlinear behavior in its magnetic circuits as well as geometric properties, particularly in the air gap, which undergoes variations depending on the rotation mode. To tackle this non-linear challenge, the finite element method is utilized as an effective approach for modeling and resolving the issue at hand. The paper investigates two cases regarding the magnetic characteristics of the SRM. The first case involves considering numerous linear states of permeability derived from the non-linear curve B = f (H), while the second case encompasses analyzing the complete non-linear curve B = f (H). The static characteristics of the SRM are modeled using a two-dimensional finite element approach, taking into account different rotor positions corresponding to changes in electric current (excitation). Based on the comparative study results, the analysis of the two cases reveals the significance of recognizing nonlinear effects in the switched reluctance machine (SRM). The obtained results highlight the importance of accounting for nonlinearity in SRM modeling. The evaluation of these features is conducted through the finite element modeling process in two scenarios. The first case focuses on considering the nonlinearity of the geometry, specifically the variance in the air gap. The second case takes into account the nonlinear properties of the components, including nonlinear magnetic circuits, coupled with non-linear geometries. By examining these two cases, the research sheds light on the importance of incorporating non-linear considerations in SRM analysis.

articleTitle: Cascaded Structure of L-Section Composite Right/Left Handed Transmission Line as Matching Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: in this work, a new iterative method to evaluate the different parameter of composite right left-handed transmission lines (CRLH TL) is applied, in .the aim to define the scattering parameters of a given number N of CRLH TL unit cells mounted in cascade. Starting from the first unit ABCD parameter one can extract the whole cascade ABCD parameters, furthermore the scattering parameter S of the cascade structure are easily extracted. Based on the results of this new method, the cascade structure of CRLH TL is used as broadband matching circuit. The numerical results are given and discussed, then compared to simulation on HFSS.

articleTitle: Enhanced Triple Band Circular Coplanar Microstrip Patch Antenna Using Complementary Split Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents a triple-band circular coplanar microstrip antenna based on Complementary Split Ring Resonators (CSRR) operating at three frequency bands: 3.07 GHz-4.83 GHz, 5.18 GHz-5.45 GHz, and 5.84 GHz-9.46 GHz. The antenna design aims to improve performance in terms of impedance bandwidth, gain, and reflection coefficient. The conventional antenna exhibits a single resonance frequency at 3.9 GHz with a modest gain of 1.60 dBi and a lower reflection coefficient of -41.13 dB. To achieve multiband characteristics, CSRR, a metamaterial (MTM) structure, is incorporated into the patch and feed line of the antenna. Simulation results using CST Microwave Studio show two additional resonance frequencies at 5.31 GHz and 9.09 GHz, with the lowest reflection coefficients of -27.78 dB and -50.22 dB, and higher gains of 1.07 dBi and 3.76 dBi, respectively. The proposed antenna design provides a compact solution for multiple frequency bands, making it suitable for satellite communication and radar systems for weather and aircraft, as well as WLAN (Wi-Fi 5, Wi-Fi 6E) applications.

articleTitle: Enhancing Battery Degradation Prediction using Recurrent and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In the field of battery technology, the ability to predict degradation accurately is of paramount importance.This study aims to develop and assess a data-driven prognostics framework for forecasting capacity and power fade in lithium-ion batteries. Leveraging machine learning techniques, specifically recurrent neural networks (RNNs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs), this framework models the intricate relationships between battery performance and aging effects. Through the utilization of historical battery data, it facilitates accurate predictions of future degradation trends. The performance of the models is meticulously evaluated using relevant metrics, including the Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean absolute error (MAE). Furthermore, the paper provides a comparative analysis to gauge the accuracy and efficacy of RNNs and CNNs models for battery prognostics, contributing to a deeper understanding of their respective capabilities. It is demonstrated that RNNs excel in predicting both resistance and capacitance degradation. These findings have the potential to significantly enhance the precision and efficiency of battery degradation predictions, with broad applications across industries.

articleTitle: Mathematical Optimization Approach for Multi-row Facility Layout Problem Under Order Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Facility layout problem (FLP) is a key area of research and development in industrial engineering. It is a combinatorial optimization problem defined as the search for the most efficient layout of facilities on the ground floor. FLPS can be classified according to different aspects. Among the most studied FLPs, we find FLPs on rows.In this work we’re interested to Multi-row facility layout problem (MRFLP) where facilities must be assigned to rows, each facility is located entirely within a row without overlapping with other facilities. The aim of our contribution is to elaborate a mathematical model with the objective of minimizing material flow distance under order constraint. The purpose is to provide solutions for small instances of the MRFLP using Cplex solver. The results demonstrate that the model is able to achieve good objective function values in a short time.

articleTitle: Facial recognition and detection using Convolution Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Pattern and facial recognition solutions are one of the biometric recognition technologies that are based on processing information of facial features. Here, we aimed to develop a classification model for face recognition of 400 images collected in the AT&T face (ORL) database. The set images were taken in the laboratory between April 1992 and April 1994 from 40 distinct people with several lighting, facial expressions, and facial characteristics. The developed model is based on the improved technique CNN and trained on 400 images of 40 persons in 10 different aspects (lighting, glasses, smiling, closed/open eyes). The accuracy achieved by the developed CNN model reached 99.04% for the majority of classes. To conclude, the proposed classification models provided important information with the highest accuracy for face recognition. These developed models and strategies could lead to the recognition of faces for several reasons (security, matching, recognition, and so forth) to detect criminals, unknown employees, or attendees.

articleTitle: Observer Design for Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Systems Using Poly-Quadratic Lyapunov Function Based On Lipschitz Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this work, a contribution to reduce the conservatism of the observers for Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy systems with unmeasurable premise variables (UPV) based on the Lipschitz assumption compared to previous work is proposed. In order to achieve this goal, the poly-quadratic Lyapunov function (PQLF) along with a good employment of the completion of squares property are used. The proposed method helps in reducing the conservatism that arises when the Lipschitz constant exceeds an admissible value and when the quadratic approach becomes infeasible. The stability conditions are presented as Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs), ensuring the asymptotic convergence of the state estimation error. A numerical illustration is provided to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed work.

articleTitle: FPGA Hardware in the Loop Validation of Fuzzy MCSA current analysis-based fault diagnostic of induction motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Currently, the analysis of the stator current signal of induction motors (known as MCSA) has gained popularity as a method to evaluate the operational condition of asynchronous motors and prevent potential breakdowns. Traditional approaches for detecting faults in rotating machinery, relying on micro-programmed sequential systems like microprocessors and DSPs, have demonstrated its limits in terms of real-time requirements and processing speed. To address these challenges, it has become essential to embrace cutting-edge technologies, such as ASICs or FPGAs, which offer more efficient diagnostic capabilities. The innovation in our research lies in the development of a fault detection algorithm implemented on FPGA hardware architecture for a induction machines. This algorithm leverages fuzzy logic and analyzes the stator current signal (MCSA), specifically by considering the "Root Mean Square" (RMS) of the stator current as an indicator of potential faults. To validate this architecture, we conducted hardware in the loop validation procedure using Xilinx Virtex-4 ML402 FPGA board and XSG within the Matlab/Simulink environment. Our hardware architecture has significantly enhanced the fault detection performance in induction machines, notably in terms of online real-time detection, detection speed, and resource utilization.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Numerical Relay to Provide Current and Voltage Protection for Electric Networks Using Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive overview of the design, simulation, and real-time implementation of a numerical relay that provides overcurrent and over/undervoltage protection for power transmission and distribution networks. The Safety of the electrical network is greatly reliant on protective relays, with a particular emphasis on the IDMT (Inverse Definite Minimum Time) overcurrent relay. The IDMT relay is required to effectively isolate any faulty component from the operational system in the event of any issues or abnormalities. Additionally, ensuring stable operation in a power system necessitates the implementation of over/under voltage protection as a crucial aspect. The protection strategy implemented aims to mitigate potential harm to the power systems by effectively isolating faulty components. To ensure the prevention of overcurrent and overload issues, a conventional IDMT relay is employed. Additionally, voltage protection is ensured through the utilization of an inverse time delay relay. However, the proposed numerical relay offers the advantage of providing both protections at a reduced cost. To validate the efficacy of the coordinated control and protection process, Matlab/Simulink simulations have been conducted under different operating scenarios. CT and PT are utilized as current and voltage sensors, while the Raspberry Pi is programmed to execute the appropriate IDMT relay, including Standard Inverse-SI, very inverse-VI, and Extreme inverse-EI, as well as the Inverse time delay relay. The implementation and testing of IEEE/ANSI Codes 50 (Instantaneous Overcurrent Relay), 51 (AC Inverse Time Overcurrent Relay), 27 (Undervoltage Relay), and 59 (Overvoltage Relay) in accordance with IEC 60255 are conducted under diverse fault conditions.

Author Keywords: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Extreme Learning Machine and Backpropagation for Faults Diagnosis in the Tennessee Eastman Process
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper explores a comparative analysis of two learning algorithms: the Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) and the Back-Propagation (BP), specifically applied to the Single Layer Feed-Forward (SLFF) neural network. To conduct this investigation, we have selected the Tennessee Eastman Process (TEP) as a case study. The evaluation criteria encompass the time demands and accuracy levels during both the learning and testing phases.The results reveals that SLFF, when trained using BP, achieves superior accuracy and demonstrates faster performance in both the learning and testing phases when compared to its training with ELM.

articleTitle: Control and Stabilization of Chaotic Systems Using Lyapunov Stability Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper proposes the application of Lyapunov stability theory for controlling and stabilizing chaotic systems. The system's chaotic behavior is mastered through a suitable Lyapunov function and control law, leading to rapid convergence toward a stable equilibrium. The study also investigates the effects of time-delayed control law on system stabilization. The numerical simulations validated the proposed approach and showed its efficiency to control, successfully, the system's chaotic behavior, and its potential for practical applications in various chaotic systems.

articleTitle: Miniaturized antenna for cognitive communication in the IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this paper, we present an in-depth study on the design and simulation of a miniaturized antenna specifically designed for cognitive communications in IoT applications. Utilizing CST software, we conducted simulations and optimizations on the antenna's performance, targeting a central frequency of 5.8 GHz—a standard in both wireless networks and IoT communications.Our design methodology follows an iterative approach, wherein we fine-tune antenna parameters to attain optimal performance in gain, directivity, reflection coefficient, and efficiency. We additionally addressed miniaturization constraints by implementing geometric modifications in the ground plane and patch to facilitate seamless integration into IoT devices.The simulation results unequivocally demonstrate the miniaturized antenna's outstanding performance, delivering both a commendable gain and adequate directivity, all the while maintaining a compact form factor with a 27% reduction in size. These attributes position it as an excellent choice for IoT devices where space and power consumption are critical considerations.

articleTitle: Numerical and Experimental Analyzis of Nonlinear Characteristics of a 12/8 Switched Reluctance Machine for Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In This paper, we examine the design and the manufacture of a 12/8 switched reluctance machine for a frequency conversion machine. In this case, a nonlinear mathematical model based on finite elements method is proposed. The obtained results of the nonlinear magnetic properties from the Ansys software are compared and validated with the realized practical ones. By analyzing the inductance variations in terms of currents and positions of the moving part in both linear and nonlinear cases, a significant difference between the maximum and the minimum inductance values is, clearly, observed. Based on these so important findings, it can be concluded that a machine with such capabilities can function as both a motor and a generator and providing additional energy. Additionally, our analysis study aims essentially to facilitate the control and enhance the performances of the switched reluctance machine under various torque loads.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Mechanical Speed Regulation Reliability Of Artificial Intelligent PSO-FLC Control
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: this paper addresses modeling and control of a wind energy conversion system (WECS). The WECS based on Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator, PMSG. Wind energy transformed to mechanical energy via blade and turbine to give speed and torque to the PMSG. This mechanical speed will be controlled firstly with a classical MPPT-PI then will be optimized by a PSO algorithm, after that a new intelligent controller MPPT-FLC will be applied to show the efficiency of that's kind of controller on our WECS mechanical speed control. The analysis and discussion of the simulation results aim to enhance the reliability and efficiency of each suggested approach. Keywords—Wind turbine, Speed control, Optimization, FLC, PSO, PI.

articleTitle: Spatial profiles evaluations of negative nitrogen corona discharge performances
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Plasma is a state of material in addition to solid, liquid and gaseous states. It is possible to benefit from the energy of the substance according to its chemical state, but the state of plasma has been very popular in various fields such as renewable energy, medicine and space science. Plasma exists naturally in the universe and can be prepared in a laboratory using heat or electricity. The study of plasma can be divided into three aspects, the first of which is theoretical, which explains the various physicochemical phenomena mathematically with equations, hypotheses, and guesses, and the second is the experimental technical aspect, which is the most difficult in practice due to its cost and sensitivity. As for the third aspect, which we will rely on in this paper, it is simulation. We chose the corona discharge technique to model the effective chemical reactions in the field of nitrogen plasma production under atmospheric pressure, extra high temperature, and sufficient applied voltage. Electron density, positive ion density, and negative ion density were measured spatially. The electron temperature, The electric potential and the reduced electric field curves are plotted. The results showed that it is difficult to predict the densities of the three elements due to the many intervening and influencing factors.

articleTitle: Robust Observer for Takagi-Sugeno Systems based on ℒ2-attenuation approach: Application to Separately Excited DC Motor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis and design of a robust observer for a Separately Excited DC Motor (SE-DCM), employing Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy representation to address the nonlinear complexity of the system. Initially, the mathematical model of the SE-DCM is presented, followed by its fuzzy representation constructed via the sector non-linearity approach. Subsequently the design of the observer, utilizing the ℒ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-attenuation approach, with a central focus on the perturbations introduced by the sensor noise is presented. The stability of the error dynamics is ensured through the application of the second Lyapunov theorem, which provides stability conditions as Linear Matrix Inequalities (LMIs). The effectiveness of this observer design is validated through simulation tests conducted on MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Convolutional Reservoir Computing for Arrhythmia Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are the foremost cause of mortality worldwide, as stated by the World Health Organization (WHO). The electrocardiogram (ECG) signal is an essential tool for examining the heart’s condition and detecting early arrhythmia abnormalities, which can be life-saving. Our contribution to arrhythmia classification endeavors is a convolutional reservoir computing-based heartbeat classifier. This classifier leverages a convolution neural network (CNN) and reservoir computing (RC) to execute the classification task. The MIT-BIH database is employed to evaluate the algorithm’s validity. An overall accuracy of 99.63% is attained for the convolutional-based classifier compared to 99.32% for the standard RC-based classifier.

articleTitle: Fault detection in rotary agricultural machinery using genetic algorithm optimized multiple input – parallel – convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this article we propose a novel method to detect faults in agricultural rotary hay tedder, while it is working in the field, using parallel–convolutional neural networks (CNNs), designed and optimized by genetic algorithm. In this case, the problem to solve is achieving as best as possible accuracy using the genetic algorithm to utilize the optimal CNNs architecture represented by each specimen. In total, the combination of the 5 vibration signals were used as the multiple CNNs inputs. Experimental results show that our method was able to reach 80% of prediction accuracy, when classifying 7 different machine states.

articleTitle: A Review on Forest Fire Detection and Monitoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Forest fires are one of the problems that endanger the durability of the forest. The occurrence of forest fires has grown significantly throughout the globe in recent years. They are one such catastrophe that puts human and animal lives in substantial risk; it also devastates woodland vegetation. The identification of forest fires as quickly as possible with precise localization and early alerting to fire units being critical. Several detection and monitoring systems have been suggested to achieve this goal, these include observers in monitoring towers, aerial and satellite monitoring, detection, and monitoring systems based on optical camera sensors, and other kinds of detection sensors or their combinations employing WSN (Wireless Sensor Network) technology. This paper will reveal the numerous methods that have been utilized to detect forest fires, each methodology has its own set of benefits and drawbacks. After comparing the various methods, we will conclude what is the optimal method to identify a fire in its early stages.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Sliding Mode Control for a variable Speed Wind System Using DFIM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This paper, presents a study on the modeling and control of a doubly fed induction machine (DFIM) based on wind energy conversion system (WECS)With Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT)with the enslavement of pitch angle control. As it’s known in the literature, the control method uses a classical linear PI controller, which presents some disadvantages, such as instantaneous errors in the mechanical speed and active and reactive powers due to the stochastic nature of wind and parametric uncertainties of the machine and their variation. In order to improve the system performances by eliminating these errors while maintaining acceptable dynamic behavior, we applied in this article a non-linear robust control technique known as First-order sliding mode control (SMC). This approach is known by its precision in tracking, simplicity, stability and robustness, as for the response time it gives very low response time. The chattering phenomenon of the SMC approach that appear as fluctuations in the electromagnetic torque is the principal flaw of this technique, the outcomes simulation obtained with a 1.5 MW wind turbine substantiate the effectiveness and the performance of the suggested control approach.

articleTitle: A Novel Equilibrium Optimization Algorithm for Optimal Coordination of Directional Overcurrent Relays
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Short circuit protection is considered an important task to provide reliability and correct performance of power system. For this reason, it is necessary to have a good choice of settings of various settings of current directional relay, in order to assure the effectiveness of tripping of protection device. The objective of this work is to optimize of Coordination of Directional Overcurrent Relays (This is achieved by optimizing the parameters Time-Dial Setting-or TDS and Pickup Current Setting-OR PCS). The optimization method used is new metaheuristic based on a newly proposed optimization technique, namely the Equilibrium Optimization (EO) algorithm. The goal of this study is to minimize the total operation time of all primary relays required to eliminate faults within their respective regions. This study was realized on IEEE 4-bus, 8-bus, and 15-bus networks under MATLAB2023a. The obtained results are compared with similar works in the literature. Results obtained demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach towards the minimization of the relay running time for an optimal coordination of Directional Overcurrent Relays (DOCRs).

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Classification of Diabetes Disease: A Case Study with Orange Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Timely diagnosis plays a pivotal role in saving lives, necessitating the integration of artificial intelligence with medical data to achieve real-time accuracy. In this research, a variety of Machine Learning algorithms, including Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, K-nearest neighbors, and Decision Tree, were applied to detect diabetes using the PIMA Indians diabetes dataset comprising 9 attributes and 768 cases. The primary objective of this study is to compare the performance of these classification algorithms. The evaluation was based on key metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, F1 score, and Recall. The machine learning models exhibited commendable accuracy, particularly with the Random Forest algorithm achieving 97% accuracy, the Decision Tree reaching 95% accuracy, the Support Vector Machines attaining 86% accuracy, and the K-nearest neighbors demonstrating 85% accuracy.

articleTitle: PV Module Reconfiguration Method Based on Battle Royale Optimization Algorithm for Output Power Improvement under Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) modules are widely used for generating clean energy, but their performance may be adversely affected by partial shading. This paper proposes an effective reconfiguration method to enhance the power generation of solar PV modules under partial shading conditions (PSCs). This method introduces the Battle Royale Optimization (BRO) algorithm to achieve the PV array optimal configuration. The BRO algorithm can effectively explore the solution space and avoid local optima, resulting in a significant improvement in the PV output power. The performance of the proposed approach based on the BRO algorithm is compared with other existing methods through both simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink and experimental outcomes on a PV station in Ain El-Melh, Algeria. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms other existing methods in terms of output power enhancement under different PSCs.

articleTitle: Model-Free Predictive Current Control for Voltage Source Inverter: A Comparative Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive comparative investigation between the Model-Free Predictive Control (MFPC) approach based on an Ultra-Local Model (ULM) and conventional Model Predictive Control (MPC) within the context of a two-level voltage-source inverter (2L-VSI). The MFPC strategy harnesses historical data and the ULM for enhanced adaptability in uncertain scenarios. Simulation results reveal that the MFPC approach, employing Algebraic Identification Approaches (API), Extended State Observer (ESO), and Integral sliding mode observer (ISMO), maintains commendable performance under steady-state conditions, even when encountering parameter mismatches. Notably, during quick changes in current reference, the MFPC approach, specifically MFPCC-ISMO, showcases superior dynamic performance. Furthermore, when contrasted with MFPC and conventional MPC methods, the ULM-augmented strategy exhibits notable superiority. The incorporation of the ULM substantiates the MFPC's efficacy, supporting robust power conversion systems conducive to the transition to cleaner and sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: Improved YOLOv5s for Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: The utilization of deep learning technology for object detection offers the notable benefit of attaining high levels of accuracy. The level of accuracy attained is contingent upon the duration of processing time required by the deep learning technology. The algorithm for object detection is commonly referred to as You Only Look Once (YOLO). This study presents a novel object detection algorithm utilizing the Yolov5 framework, coupled with a substantial dataset. The improvement of YOLOv5 commenced with the incorporation of the Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast module (SPPF) into the yolov5s neck network to extract multiple scale image features. Then, the depth of the backbone SPPF module has been raised from 1024 to 2048 to improve accuracy. The modified YOLOV5 model was utilized for object detection, resulting in the extraction of object information categorized into seven distinct classes. The achieved results include a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.821 at an intersection over union (IoU) threshold of 0.5, and a mAP of 0.386 within the IoU range of 0.5 to 0.95, with a precision value of 0.761. Additionally, a recall value of 0.769 was obtained. The application of our research framework has demonstrated its effectiveness in enhancing the performance of object detection algorithms.

articleTitle: Performance comparison of three deep learning techniques applied to the fault detection of a transmission network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: This study highlights the development of intelligent techniques (decision trees DT, support vector machines SVM and deep learning DL) to solve the issue of fault detection and location in transmission networks. These techniques are developed using both MATLAB and Python programming languages and tested considering an IEEE 39-bus standard test network. thirteen cases of faults are investigated. Further examination of performances (both accuracy and rapidity) of these methods are carried out to identify the most beneficial approach. The assessment of the studied methods achievements highlighted the effectiveness of the DL approach, which achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 100%. However, the convergence time of the DL algorithm (0.9 seconds), as obtained from various tests, surpassed other algorithms. Nevertheless, when considering different results acquired through testing on other standard networks (IEEE 14-bus and IEEE 09-bus), it becomes evident that, unlike the DT and SVM algorithms, the convergence time of the DL algorithm decreases as the volume of data increases.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Strategies for Solar Irradiation Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In this work, we conduct a comparative analysis of Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) approaches for solar irradiation forecasting at Batna station. Specifically, we examine six different ML methods: Linear Regression (LR), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). Furthermore, we investigate a deep learning-based regression approach considered a relatively recent field technique. We propose to use three DL methods, namely Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM). We present and discuss the experimental outcomes obtained from the Batna station data.

articleTitle: Protection of multi-biometric data based on deep learning and BioHashing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Multi-biometrics is a nascent technological advancement that augments the process of individual authentication and identification via the use of numerous biometric modalities. Nevertheless, the susceptibility of multi-biometric systems lies in the difficulty of revoking biometric templates in the event of theft, hence giving rise to substantial apprehensions over privacy and security. In order to tackle this issue, a protection mechanism has been devised using a technique known as "Biohashing," which enables the reversible alteration of biometric characteristics. This particular method provides protection for the biometric template and enables the ability to revoke it if deemed appropriate. The proposed approach incorporates a biometric characteristic, namely fingerprints (referred to as instance 1 and instance 2), via the use of deep learning-based feature extraction, which is then followed by score fusion. The acquired findings illustrate the resilience of the "Biohashing" protection technique, successfully attaining a 0% error rate.

articleTitle: Friendly Deep Learning Model for Estimating Daily Global Solar Radiation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Technologies have transformed our life: work, social life, economy and communicates, making with it a slew of new conveniences, efficiency, and connection. However, all of these wonderful advantages have resulted in an increase in energy usage. As a result, various attempts are being undertaken to make technologies more energy-efficient and to power these technical infrastructures using renewable energies such as : wind ,water and solar power. To effectively use solar energy and foresee its future, large investments in green energy research and development are required. In line with this goal, it is required to evaluate the potential of solar energy using a variety of models when forecasting and estimating it. We estimate global sun radiation on a horizontal surface in this article. These models' inputs are meteorological parameters and data. LSTM (Long and Short Term Memory Neural Networks),CNN (Convolutional Neural Networks), RNN (Recurrent Neural Networks) and MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) are the Deep Learning methods used in this work, and the impact of the parameter optimizer was investigated. The dataset for this study were obtained from the Helio-Clim1 site and span a ten-year period (1996 to 2005). Among the performance requirements for solar radiation forecasting models are forecast accuracy, model resilience, predictor uncertainty, and predictor dependability. Finally, in terms of error values, the CNN model outperforms the others (MAE=2,00, MSE=7,66, RMSE = 2,67, and R2 = 0,86).

articleTitle: Determination of the best wind blade shape adopted to Reynolds number
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Wind rotor efficiency is based on the high performance of their parts. The blade is classed first as the essential part that is responsible for collecting wind energy. That is related to geometry which is a combination of section form, chord, and twist distribution. The section shape in general is an airfoil. In this work, an evaluation study has been established based on Matlab code and Qblade software. In which new distribution of chord and twist angle have been defined based on variation of Reynolds number in aim to maximum energy production. A 5KW wind rotor was proposed to evaluate the best distribution with the NACA2412 OF airfoil section intended to be installed on the Adrar, Hassi R’mel, Tindouf, and Ain Salah zones. The results show that the model adopted to Reynolds numbers greater than 1e6 gave the best annual production with maximum gain registered by the model adopted to 1.2e6 of Reynolds number.

articleTitle: Enhanced Multi-Target Surveillance and Tracking Algorithm for Collaborative Drones in IoT Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: In the realm of IoT-enabled surveillance systems, drones play a pivotal role in detecting and tracking suspects within defined areas. However, a significant challenge arises when a single drone identifies multiple suspects concurrently, leading to the inability to effectively track all targets simultaneously. To address this limitation, this paper introduces a collaborative algorithm designed to enhance multi-target surveillance and tracking in such environments. The algorithm fosters cooperation among drones by dynamically selecting suitable assisting drones to engage in the tracking process. When a drone identifies multiple suspects, it transmits relevant information, including positional data and imagery, to the base station. Subsequently, the algorithm orchestrates the assignment of new tracking missions to assisting drones, enabling them to effectively follow the additional targets. This paper elucidates the algorithm’s intricate workings, elucidates its integration within the IoT-based surveillance system architecture, and presents the empirical results of its implementation. Through experimental evaluation, we demonstrate the algorithm’s efficacy in improving tracking accuracy, mission success rate, and resource utilization. The proposed solution holds the potential to revolutionize multi-target tracking capabilities in IoT-driven surveillance scenarios, offering a tangible advancement in collaborative drone operations.

articleTitle: A Statistically Efficient Method for Fusion of Multimodal Images in NSCT Domain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Advanced Technology (ICEEAT)
abstract: Image fusion is a procedure that enhances the understanding of a scene by integrating information collected from various imaging sensors. This technique is extensively applied in the field of image processing due to its effectiveness. Multifocus image fusion is a technique that deals with the challenge of combining two or more images captured of the same scene but focused on different depths. In medical image fusion, the primary benefit is the ability to extract relevant data from input images captured by different devices for the same organ, which is very useful for disease diagnosis. This concept of image processing holds significant importance across various applications as it contributes to improved perception, decision-making, and overall system performance.In the present study, we propose an efficient algorithm based on the non-subsampled contourlet transform (NSCT). This method takes into consideration the strong linear dependency between high-frequency coefficients in the input images. The low-frequency coefficients are fused using different fusion rules based on principal component analysis and a salience match measure. We conducted experiments using three sets of multimodal images, and the performance of our algorithm is compared to various spatial and transform domain image fusion methods presented in existing literature. We employed quantitative evaluation techniques based on diverse image fusion quality criteria to assess the fusion results. Additionally, we conducted subjective assessments to gauge the performance of the resulting fused images.
